subject: SignalVault pricing ask — proposed match & technical packaging

Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — pricing alignment + runtime fit questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — team loved the latency profile on short-chat and the embedding recall. We’re finalizing a vendor decision for an inference contract that will run our customer-facing chat for ~18 months. Our procurement team has a competing offer that is ~28% cheaper for the first 12 months and includes a modest migration credit.

Before we move forward with them, two asks:
1) Can Redwood match or come within 10% on TCO for year 1 (including any pilot/credits)? We’re focused on unit token price + KV cache savings assumptions.
2) A short technical checklist: are there any model-variant limitations (quantization/8-bit) we should know about for the customer prompt lengths (avg 512, 95th pct 1024)? Also: how do your fallbacks behave if a dedicated pool is saturated?

I’ve attached our RFP summary and our usage projection. Would appreciate a short written offer we can show procurement by Tue 10/13.

Best,
Jared
Head of Cloud Ops
SignalVault

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@signalvault.io>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@signalvault.io>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pricing alignment + runtime fit questions

Jared — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the projections. Short answers up front: we can put together a targeted economic match that hits within 8–10% of the competitor for year 1 (pilot credit + seat-based bridge + token rebate), and technically we support the workflows you described with two packaging options (hosted with reserved throughput vs Redwood Dedicated).

High-level offer (summary):
- Pilot: 90-day pilot with a $35k credit against hosting usage.
- Year 1 pricing: blended per-token price that brings your expected monthly spend within 9% of the competitor number you sent (we’ll send the blended math sheet).
- Migration bridge: one-time onboarding credit applied over first 3 invoices (up to $25k).
- SLA: 99.9% regional availability for dedicated pools; hosted tier has 99.5% with multi-region fallbacks.

Technical notes:
- Quantization: We support int8 and a mixed-precision path that preserves 99% of accuracy for your ensembles at 512–1024 context; for 95th pct 1024 we recommend the dedicated pool (lower latency tail).
- Fallbacks: If a dedicated pool is saturated we can route to a compatible hosted variant (slightly higher per-token cost and ~10–50ms added tail latency). Prefix/KV cache warms carry across compatible variants to reduce cold-start token cost.

I’m looping in Karthik with a quick ask: can you confirm any sequence-length risk and whether we should propose an explicit SLA waiver for the 1024 tail? I’ve also included a draft commercial term we can send to legal if this looks good.

Next steps:
- Karthik: technical fit confirmation (tomorrow EOD)
- Jared/Priya: any deal-breakers to the commercial structure above?
- I’ll generate the blended math + a short MOU by Mon 10/12 EOD.

Thanks — lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: SV-quick-offer-matrix.xlsx (will attach in next mail)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick ask — pricing alignment + runtime fit questions

Lauren — quick technical confirmation based on the usage file Jared provided.

Summary:
- Avg context: 512 OK on hosted and dedicated. For repeated 1024 tails we see increased KV cache pressure and a measurable latency tail on CPUs/oversubscribed inference nodes. Dedicated GPU pool with 40% headroom will keep p95 latency within target.
- Quantization: int8 path works for the majority of your model family; recommend running a short eval (10k prompts) to validate top-k recall for your top prompt types.
- Fallthrough behavior: our routing preserves KV cache only when model variants are ABI-compatible (same tokenizer & key-layout). If you mix an int8-quantized variant and a non-quantized variant, the cache will be invalidated and you should expect higher token costs on cold starts.

Operational suggestion: propose a two-phased rollout — start hosted pilot (90 days) with the int8 mixed-precision variant + auto-scaling; then commit to Dedicated pool if post-pilot p95 latency exceeds threshold. Add an explicit 'fallback cost share' clause so SignalVault isn’t charged full delta on fallbacks during the first 60 days.

I attached a short ops checklist for onboarding and a draft SLA waiver clause to cover the 1024 tail.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: RV-onboard-checklist.pdf, SLA-waiver-1024-tail.txt
